title: Parts of the revolver
subtitle: The revolver: main parts and what they do

lines: In this episode, we learn the main parts of the revolver, and what each one does.
Just as with the pistol, you must be able to label the revolver's diagram and explain its main parts.

scenes.definition: The body of the firearm to which all the other parts are attached.
lines: On the revolver, the frame is again the body of the firearm to which all the other parts are attached.
The book compares it to the chassis of a motor vehicle.

lines.text: Here is the frame on our revolver.
And here is the barrel, a metal tube down which the bullet will travel.
Inside the barrel there are spiraling lands and grooves, known as rifling.
The rifling causes the bullet to spin.
This spinning stabilises the bullet in flight.
In the list of main parts, the revolver has a cylinder where the pistol has a slide.
The cylinder rotates to bring the new loaded chamber in line with the barrel and firing pin.
The ejector rod and the extractor star are fitted to the cylinder.
When loading and unloading, the cylinder swings out on the crane.
The cylinder contains multiple chambers, usually five or six.
The action refers to the moving parts of the firearm.
For example, the trigger.
The hammer.
And the parts that rotate the cylinder.
So on the pistol, the book's example includes the slide, and on the revolver, the parts that rotate the cylinder.
Page twenty five labels the parts of the revolver.
At the front, the muzzle, the front sight and the barrel.
Under the barrel, the ejector rod.
Then the cylinder, and the crane.
At the back, the hammer and the cylinder release.
Below, the frame, the trigger guard and the trigger.
And the grip.

lines: Here is the book's photo, with fourteen labels.
Two of them aren't on our drawing.
The top strap, above the cylinder.
And the hammer spur, on the hammer.
Learn all fourteen names: the formative exam's revolver diagram is worth fourteen marks.

scenes.question: What causes the bullet to spin?
lines: The exam asks you to explain the barrel.
What causes the bullet to spin?
reveal: The rifling: spiraling lands and grooves inside the barrel.
This spinning stabilises the bullet in flight.

lines: When loading and unloading, what does the cylinder swing out on?
reveal: The crane. When loading and unloading, the cylinder swings out on the crane.

points: Frame: the body all parts attach to
Cylinder: lines up the next loaded chamber

lines: The frame is the body, and all the other parts are attached to it.
The barrel's rifling spins the bullet, which stabilises it in flight.
The cylinder rotates to bring the new loaded chamber in line with the barrel and firing pin.
For loading and unloading, it swings out on the crane.
And the action is the moving parts: the trigger, the hammer and the parts that rotate the cylinder.
